title: Cross-vacancy fan-out bound (3 emails/recipient/hour) is TOCTOU-defeatable by concurrent claims
evidence:
AND (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
  ) < 3
detail: Concurrent claims on different vacancy rows share no lock; the count subquery reads a pre-burst snapshot. Drafts plantable unauthenticated on any public vacancy code let K concurrent claims each pass '< 3' — K branded emails/hour, not 3.
recommended_fix: Serialize per recipient: wrap count-check + stamp in a transaction holding pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(lower(email))), or a per-recipient hourly counter row taken SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.

title: resumed_at never stamped when a fully-saved draft is resumed then submitted without step navigation
evidence:
UPDATE application_draft
SET resumed_at = COALESCE(resumed_at, now())
WHERE continue_token = $1
  AND vacancy_id = $2::uuid
  AND submitted_at IS NULL
RETURNING id::text;  // mark is called only from the two save paths (draft_handler.gleam:209, :289); form_stepper.js:21 "// for. The initial show on page load deliberately does NOT dispatch."; strip_draft_on_submit.sql sets "submitted_at = now(),"
detail: Fully-saved draft resumed: no step-change fires (init doesn't dispatch; consent+submit needs no navigation), so no save runs. The pagehide beacon lands after strip sets submitted_at; the guard blocks the stamp — resumed_at never set, resume→submit undercounted.
recommended_fix: Render resume_token as a hidden form field on the resume page and have strip_draft_on_submit (or finalise_application) COALESCE resumed_at when the submitted token matches the draft being stripped.
